00374.title: Trabectedin for advanced soft tissue sarcoma
00374.context: Adult advanced soft tissue sarcoma after anthracycline and ifosfamide treatment has failed, or when those medicines are unsuitable
00374.purpose: The aim is to control advanced sarcoma and help symptoms. The strongest trial evidence concerns previously treated liposarcoma and leiomyosarcoma; the team explains expected benefit for your particular subtype.
00374.label: Trabectedin: one 24-hour infusion every 21 days

agents.name: Trabectedin
agents.explanation: Trabectedin binds to the genetic material, deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA), and interferes with how cancer cells use and repair it. This can slow tumour growth; normal blood, liver and muscle cells can also be affected.
agents.watch: Report fever, marked muscle pain or weakness, dark or reduced urine, jaundice, new swelling, breathlessness or line-site pain urgently.
risks: Low blood counts, serious infection or sepsis, anaemia and bleeding
Nausea, vomiting, appetite loss, constipation, mouth soreness and fatigue
Liver injury, sometimes severe; prescribed steroid premedication and blood checks are essential
Muscle breakdown (rhabdomyolysis), which can cause kidney failure; muscle-enzyme monitoring is required
Heart muscle injury or heart failure; leakage of fluid from small blood vessels can cause swelling and low blood pressure
Allergic reactions and severe tissue damage if treatment leaks outside the vein; fertility and pregnancy harm
visual: Blood, liver, muscle and heart checks

00374.schedule: Trabectedin 1.5 mg/m² is infused over 24 hours starting on day 1 of each 21-day cycle. Treatment continues while benefit and tolerability justify it. The actual dose, start time and any delay require a new safety review.
00374.administration: Central venous access is strongly recommended. Trained staff connect the prescribed 24-hour infusion and confirm its actual disconnection time. Dexamethasone 20 mg is given intravenously 30 minutes beforehand. The full visit includes checks, preparation and line care.
00374.baseline: Full blood count, kidney and liver tests, albumin, muscle-enzyme testing and heart pumping assessment before starting. Review infection, pre-existing heart disease, prior treatment, all medicines and pregnancy precautions.
00374.monitoring: Blood counts and liver tests before each cycle and weekly during the first two cycles, then at least once between doses under current product information. Check kidney function before cycles. Creatine phosphokinase, a muscle-injury blood test, is checked weekly for the first two cycles and at least once between doses thereafter. Heart pumping is assessed at baseline and every 2–3 months until stopping.
00374.support: Dexamethasone 20 mg intravenously 30 minutes before each infusion is required for anti-sickness treatment and appears to help reduce liver toxicity. This regimen has moderate nausea/vomiting risk; agree the complete prevention and rescue prescription without duplicate steroids. Granulocyte colony-stimulating factor, a white-cell growth factor, may be used for low counts under local policy; it is not universally required.
00374.prep: Review all medicines and supplements, especially strong liver-enzyme inhibitors or inducers, statins and other liver-toxic medicines. Avoid alcohol. Confirm steroid premedication, blood tests, pump training, line care, disconnection and verified contact numbers.
00374.access: The team chooses appropriate intravenous access and explains its care. Report pain, burning, redness or swelling during treatment immediately. If a port or peripherally inserted central catheter is used, confirm dressing, flushing, infection precautions and eventual removal arrangements. Confirm spill or leak instructions and who to call if the pump alarms, becomes disconnected or appears to finish early. Never change settings or disconnect it yourself.
00374.wider: A specialist sarcoma multidisciplinary team reviews the exact pathology, disease extent, prior treatment and your priorities. Surgery or radiotherapy can have a separate role in selected situations. Symptom control, rehabilitation and palliative care can accompany systemic treatment; they are not restricted to the end of life.
00374.scope: This is later-line single-agent trabectedin over 24 hours. It is not first-line doxorubicin plus trabectedin with maintenance, and it is not the shorter ovarian-cancer combination infusion. Severe kidney impairment, heart problems or previous serious toxicity require individual oncology/pharmacy review before treatment can continue.
00374.trial: Trabectedin versus dacarbazine in previously treated liposarcoma or leiomyosarcoma
00374.evidence: A randomised phase III trial in previously treated liposarcoma or leiomyosarcoma found longer progression-free survival with trabectedin than dacarbazine. The final analysis did not demonstrate longer overall survival. This supports a disease-control discussion, not a guarantee that treatment lengthens an individual life.
00374.caveat: The trial population had prior anthracycline and another systemic regimen. It does not establish the same benefit for every soft tissue sarcoma subtype. Survival results from first-line doxorubicin/trabectedin induction followed by maintenance belong to a different treatment strategy.
doses: Starts on day 1 and continues into day 2, for 24 hours from the actual connection time, not two full days. The team confirms professional disconnection.
00374.course: Continue while benefit and tolerability justify treatment
00374.urgent: Marked muscle pain or weakness, dark or reduced urine, new swelling or faintness, jaundice, breathlessness or infusion-site pain requires urgent assessment.
boundaries: Pretreatment gates include haemoglobin at least 9 g/dL, albumin at least 25 g/L, neutrophils at least 1.5 and platelets at least 100 ×10⁹/L, with source-specific liver and muscle-enzyme limits. Current results and previous-cycle toxicity are different inputs.
Creatinine clearance below 30 mL/min conflicts with the source organ table but fails its pretreatment gate and current product criteria; do not infer treatment clearance from a no-adjustment row.
Source cardiac delay/reduction and discontinuation wording needs clinical adjudication. Prior permanent-stop history remains relevant after numerical recovery.
The source dose ladder is 1.5 to 1.2 to 1 mg/m²; do not re-escalate after a toxicity reduction. This education is not a dose calculator.

tests.timing: At baseline and before each cycle. Current product information also specifies weekly testing during the first two cycles, then at least once between doses.

tests.timing: At baseline and before cycles; extra tests for reduced urine, dehydration, muscle injury or abnormal results.

tests.purpose: Detect muscle injury before it becomes severe.
tests.timing: At baseline, weekly during the first two cycles and at least once between doses thereafter; urgent testing for marked muscle pain, weakness or dark urine.

tests.label: Heart pumping assessment
tests.purpose: Detect treatment-related heart dysfunction.
tests.timing: Heart ultrasound (echocardiogram) or a multigated acquisition heart scan before treatment and every 2–3 months until stopping, as specified in the source complication section. Additional assessment follows symptoms and clinical risk.

tests.label: Infusion line and pump review

tests.timing: Check at connection and disconnection; report pain, swelling, leakage, fever or pump problems immediately.

tests.timing: The specialist sets scan and clinical-review timing for the tumour type, treatment aim and symptoms.

00228.title: Eribulin for unresectable liposarcoma
00228.context: Adult unresectable liposarcoma after anthracycline-containing treatment for advanced or metastatic disease, unless anthracyclines are unsuitable
00228.purpose: Eribulin aims to control liposarcoma and may help symptoms. Your consultant considers the precise subtype, prior treatment, fitness and what matters to you.
00228.label: Eribulin on days 1 and 8; repeat every 21 days

agents.name: Eribulin
agents.explanation: Eribulin blocks the growth of microtubules, the small structures a cell needs to divide. It can slow liposarcoma growth but can also affect blood production and nerves.
agents.watch: Report fever or sudden illness immediately. Report numbness, weakness or difficulty walking before another dose; palpitations, fainting or a blistering rash need urgent assessment.
risks: Low blood counts, serious infection or sepsis, anaemia and bleeding
Numbness, tingling, pain or weakness from nerve injury, sometimes lasting
Fatigue, hair loss, nausea, vomiting, mouth soreness, diarrhoea or constipation
Changes in the heart electrical recovery interval (QT), especially with other risk factors or interacting medicines
Uncommon lung inflammation or liver injury; report a persistent cough, new breathlessness or yellow eyes promptly
Rare severe blistering or peeling skin reactions; allergic reactions; fertility and pregnancy harm
visual: Blood counts and nerves need review

00228.schedule: Eribulin 1.23 mg/m², expressed as eribulin base, is given on days 1 and 8 of each 21-day cycle. The team reviews safety before each dose. Treatment continues while benefit and tolerability justify it.
00228.administration: NCCP specifies an intravenous infusion over 5 minutes in sodium chloride solution. Glucose is not used for dilution. Publications may describe the equivalent 1.4 mg/m² mesilate-salt dose; it must not be entered as 1.4 mg/m² eribulin base.
00228.baseline: Full blood count and kidney/liver tests; assess existing nerve symptoms, heart disease, rhythm risks, interacting medicines and relevant electrolytes. Establish prior anthracycline treatment or why it was unsuitable.
00228.monitoring: Check blood counts before each dose, including day 8. Kidney and liver tests are reviewed at baseline and at cycle start, with extra checks as indicated. Review nerve symptoms before further dosing. Heart tracing and electrolyte monitoring depend on rhythm risk and interacting medicines.
00228.support: This is a low nausea/vomiting-risk regimen. Agree individual anti-sickness and bowel support; NCCP lists no usual separate premedication. White-cell growth-factor support may be chosen for severe neutropenia, but there is no universal routine course.
00228.prep: Bring all medicines and report numbness, weakness, constipation, infection or fainting before treatment. Review medicines that affect heart rhythm. Arrange written contraception instructions and avoid breastfeeding during treatment.
00228.access: The team chooses appropriate intravenous access and explains its care. Report pain, burning, redness or swelling during treatment immediately. If a port or peripherally inserted central catheter is used, confirm dressing, flushing, infection precautions and eventual removal arrangements.
00228.wider: A specialist sarcoma multidisciplinary team reviews the exact pathology, disease extent, prior treatment and your priorities. Surgery or radiotherapy can have a separate role in selected situations. Symptom control, rehabilitation and palliative care can accompany systemic treatment; they are not restricted to the end of life.
00228.scope: This eribulin plan is for liposarcoma, using the European eribulin-base dose. Treatment evidence and combination partners used for breast cancer are a separate clinical plan. Do not change the dose or add another cancer medicine yourself.
00228.trial: Eribulin versus dacarbazine: prespecified liposarcoma subgroup
00228.evidence: In the prespecified liposarcoma subgroup of a randomised trial, eribulin improved overall survival compared with dacarbazine. Participants had advanced dedifferentiated, myxoid/round-cell or pleomorphic liposarcoma and at least two previous systemic regimens.
00228.caveat: Trial eligibility was narrower than the licensed indication. The result is not an individual prognosis and must not be generalised to leiomyosarcoma, all sarcomas or breast cancer. The trial salt dose is equivalent to the European base dose, not a higher prescribed base dose.
doses: Eribulin base 1.23 mg/m² over 5 minutes after safety review.
Separate day 8 blood-count and symptom review before dosing.
00228.course: Continue while benefit and tolerability justify treatment
00228.urgent: Palpitations, fainting, severe blistering or peeling rash needs urgent assessment. Report new numbness, weakness or difficulty walking before another dose.
boundaries: Initial eligibility and day 1/day 8 withholding thresholds differ; current counts cannot substitute for previous-cycle nadir and complication history.

Creatinine clearance exactly 50 mL/min lies between the source greater-than/less-than rows; specialist review is required. Do not serially multiply original-dose percentages or re-escalate after reduction.
No US day-15 catch-up instruction is imported. A delayed or omitted dose needs a new locally prescribed schedule.

00205.title: Pegylated liposomal doxorubicin for metastatic soft tissue sarcoma
00205.context: Metastatic soft tissue sarcoma: the separate sarcoma indication of shared regimen 00205
00205.purpose: Treatment aims to control metastatic sarcoma and help symptoms. A specialist considers tumour subtype, previous treatment, heart risk and your priorities; benefit is uncertain for an individual.
00205.label: Pegylated liposomal doxorubicin 50 mg/m² on day 1 every 28 days

agents.name: Pegylated liposomal doxorubicin
agents.mechanism: Delivers doxorubicin in coated fat particles
agents.explanation: Doxorubicin damages the genetic material, deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA). In this formulation it is carried in tiny coated fat particles called liposomes, changing its distribution and side-effect pattern. It remains capable of causing heart injury and cannot be substituted for other doxorubicin formulations.
agents.watch: Report painful palms or soles, mouth ulcers and persistent oral lesions early. Report fever or new breathlessness urgently, and tell staff immediately about chest or throat tightness during an infusion.
risks: Painful red or blistered palms and soles (hand–foot syndrome), sometimes severe enough to limit everyday activities
Mouth soreness or ulcers that can impair eating and drinking; persistent mouth lesions require assessment
Low blood counts, serious infection, anaemia and bleeding; fatigue, nausea and bowel effects
Infusion reactions, sometimes serious; line leakage can damage tissue
Heart damage, including delayed injury; previous anthracycline exposure and cardiac disease matter
Lung inflammation; rare later blood cancers or oral cancers; fertility and pregnancy harm
visual: Mouth, skin, blood and heart checks

00205.schedule: Pegylated liposomal doxorubicin 50 mg/m² is given on day 1 every 28 days. NCCP describes typically 6 cycles or continuation until progression or unacceptable toxicity; the team confirms duration and review points.
00205.administration: The pharmacy prepares only the pegylated liposomal formulation in glucose 5%; trained staff administer it without an in-line filter. NCCP specifies a first infusion rate of 1 mg/min and later 60-minute infusions if tolerated; a previous reaction requires a supervised modified sequence. The total visit includes blood tests, review, observation and line care.
00205.baseline: Full blood count, kidney and liver tests, electrocardiogram (heart tracing) and heart pumping assessment. Review previous anthracyclines, heart disease, prior chest radiotherapy, mouth and skin condition. The source sarcoma performance-status range is 0–2, distinct from its other cancer indications.
00205.monitoring: Blood counts and kidney/liver tests before cycles; regular heart tracings. Review mouth, palms and soles before further treatment. Heart pumping assessment follows clinical risk and must precede each additional dose taking lifetime anthracycline exposure above 450 mg/m².
00205.support: NCCP classifies this as low nausea/vomiting risk and lists no usual premedication. Follow individual anti-sickness and mouth-care advice. For 4–7 days after treatment, avoid excessive heat, friction and tight pressure on hands or feet; cooling measures and any skin treatment follow the local plan. Do not start routine vitamin or steroid hand–foot prophylaxis yourself.
00205.prep: Confirm the exact pegylated liposomal product and all previous anthracycline doses. Report heart symptoms, mouth ulcers and painful hands or feet before the visit. Review interacting medicines, pregnancy precautions and any prior infusion reaction.
00205.access: The team chooses appropriate intravenous access and explains its care. Report pain, burning, redness or swelling during treatment immediately. If a port or peripherally inserted central catheter is used, confirm dressing, flushing, infection precautions and eventual removal arrangements.
00205.wider: A specialist sarcoma multidisciplinary team reviews the exact pathology, disease extent, prior treatment and your priorities. Surgery or radiotherapy can have a separate role in selected situations. Symptom control, rehabilitation and palliative care can accompany systemic treatment; they are not restricted to the end of life.
00205.scope: This is the 50 mg/m², 28-day metastatic-sarcoma context. Current Caelyx European indications do not list general soft tissue sarcoma, so the off-label rationale and consent require documentation under local policy. Breast and gynaecological efficacy claims are not transferred here. Pegylated liposomal doxorubicin is not interchangeable with conventional doxorubicin or non-pegylated liposomal Myocet.
00205.trial: EORTC randomised phase II study: liposomal versus conventional doxorubicin in advanced sarcoma
00205.evidence: A small historical randomised phase II study compared pegylated liposomal doxorubicin 50 mg/m² every four weeks with conventional doxorubicin 75 mg/m² every three weeks in advanced sarcoma. Observed response rates were similar, with different toxicity patterns: less severe neutropenia and hair loss but more hand–foot toxicity with the liposomal treatment.
00205.caveat: This was a small phase II trial with an older mixed-sarcoma population, including gastrointestinal stromal tumours. It does not prove modern non-inferiority or a survival advantage, and does not support this chemotherapy as a present-day gastrointestinal stromal tumour recommendation. Breast/ovarian outcomes are separate.
doses: 50 mg/m² after safety review; confirm the product, prescribed infusion rate and any reaction plan.
00205.urgent: Chest or throat tightness during infusion needs immediate staff attention. New breathlessness, fever, painful blistered hands or feet, or mouth ulcers preventing drinking needs urgent advice.
boundaries: The two pegylated liposomal regimens have different count thresholds; do not import the 50 mg/m² source recovery table into the 20 mg/m² schedule.
A lifetime anthracycline exposure above 450 mg/m² triggers heart pumping assessment before every additional dose; it is not an automatic stop threshold for this formulation.
Hand–foot and mouth-toxicity actions depend on current grade, worst previous grade and delay duration. Recovered symptoms do not erase a prior permanent-stop decision.
Source bilirubin bands leave a 50–51 micromol/L gap. Percentages refer to the original dose, and restart or combined-toxicity decisions need prescription reconciliation.

tests.timing: At baseline and before each cycle. The 20 mg/m² and 50 mg/m² regimens have different source count decisions; additional checks follow symptoms and prior results.

tests.label: Tumour response, symptoms and function

tests.timing: The specialist sets scan and clinical-review timing for the tumour type, treatment aim and symptoms.

Heart injury remains possible with liposomal treatment. Report breathlessness, swelling, chest pain or palpitations.
Blood tests detect liver effects. Yellow eyes, dark urine or new significant upper abdominal pain needs prompt assessment.
New cough or breathlessness needs urgent review. Tell staff immediately about chest or throat tightness during infusion.

Report persistent diarrhoea or constipation, severe pain, abdominal swelling or inability to drink.

00462.title: Pegylated liposomal doxorubicin for AIDS-related Kaposi sarcoma
00462.context: AIDS-related Kaposi sarcoma with a CD4 helper T-cell (infection-fighting immune-cell) count below 200 cells/mm³ and extensive disease of skin or mucous membranes, or internal organs
00462.purpose: Treatment aims to reduce Kaposi disease, symptoms and complications while care for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) continues. The oncology and HIV teams coordinate the plan.
00462.label: Pegylated liposomal doxorubicin 20 mg/m² on day 1 every 21 days

agents.name: Pegylated liposomal doxorubicin
agents.mechanism: Delivers doxorubicin in coated fat particles
agents.explanation: Doxorubicin damages the genetic material, deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA). In this formulation it is carried in tiny coated fat particles called liposomes, changing its distribution and side-effect pattern. It remains capable of causing heart injury and cannot be substituted for other doxorubicin formulations.
agents.watch: Report painful palms or soles, mouth ulcers and persistent oral lesions early. Report fever or new breathlessness urgently, and tell staff immediately about chest or throat tightness during an infusion.
risks: Painful red or blistered palms and soles (hand–foot syndrome), sometimes severe enough to limit everyday activities
Mouth soreness or ulcers that can impair eating and drinking; persistent mouth lesions require assessment
Low blood counts, serious infection, anaemia and bleeding; fatigue, nausea and bowel effects
Infusion reactions, sometimes serious; line leakage can damage tissue
Heart damage, including delayed injury; previous anthracycline exposure and cardiac disease matter
Lung inflammation; rare later blood cancers or oral cancers; fertility and pregnancy harm
visual: Mouth, skin, blood and heart checks

00462.schedule: Pegylated liposomal doxorubicin 20 mg/m² is given on day 1 every 21 days. NCCP specifies a maximum of 6 cycles or earlier stopping for progression or unacceptable toxicity. A 14-day interval is a separately selected alternative and must be written into the personal prescription.
00462.administration: The pharmacy prepares only the pegylated liposomal formulation in glucose 5%; trained staff administer it without an in-line filter. NCCP specifies a first infusion rate of 1 mg/min and later 60-minute infusions if tolerated; a previous reaction requires a supervised modified sequence. The current European product information instead specifies a 30-minute infusion for AIDS-related Kaposi sarcoma. Oncology and pharmacy must reconcile this with the NCCP instructions and confirm the individual infusion plan; this page does not silently choose between them.
00462.baseline: Full blood count, kidney and liver tests, electrocardiogram (heart tracing) and heart pumping assessment. Review previous anthracyclines, heart disease, prior chest radiotherapy, mouth and skin condition. Check lactate dehydrogenase, a blood marker of cell turnover, and review the Kaposi/HIV treatment context.
00462.monitoring: Blood counts and kidney/liver tests before cycles; regular heart tracings. Review mouth, palms and soles before further treatment. Heart pumping assessment follows clinical risk and must precede each additional dose taking lifetime anthracycline exposure above 450 mg/m². Repeat lactate dehydrogenase only when indicated; HIV and immune monitoring follow the specialist plan.
00462.support: NCCP classifies this as low nausea/vomiting risk and lists no usual premedication. Follow individual anti-sickness and mouth-care advice. For 4–7 days after treatment, avoid excessive heat, friction and tight pressure on hands or feet; cooling measures and any skin treatment follow the local plan. Do not start routine vitamin or steroid hand–foot prophylaxis yourself.
00462.prep: Confirm the exact pegylated liposomal product and all previous anthracycline doses. Report heart symptoms, mouth ulcers and painful hands or feet before the visit. Review interacting medicines, pregnancy precautions and any prior infusion reaction. Coordinate antiretroviral medicines and opportunistic-infection prevention with the HIV team; chemotherapy does not replace that care.
00462.access: The team chooses appropriate intravenous access and explains its care. Report pain, burning, redness or swelling during treatment immediately. If a port or peripherally inserted central catheter is used, confirm dressing, flushing, infection precautions and eventual removal arrangements.
00462.wider: AIDS means acquired immunodeficiency syndrome. HIV-directed treatment and assessment for opportunistic infections remain essential. Local treatment can suit selected Kaposi lesions; the team decides whether systemic chemotherapy is needed and reconciles the product restriction where local therapy or systemic alfa-interferon could effectively treat the disease.
00462.scope: This is the 20 mg/m² Kaposi schedule, normally every 21 days, with an explicitly selected 14-day alternative. It is not the 50 mg/m² sarcoma or breast schedule. The infusion-duration disagreement needs oncology/pharmacy resolution. Pegylated liposomal doxorubicin is not interchangeable with conventional doxorubicin or non-pegylated liposomal Myocet.
00462.trial: Pegylated liposomal doxorubicin versus bleomycin/vincristine in Kaposi sarcoma
00462.evidence: A historical randomised trial in HIV-related Kaposi sarcoma compared the 20 mg/m² every-three-week schedule for six cycles with bleomycin/vincristine. Tumour responses were more frequent with liposomal doxorubicin; neutropenia and delays remained important.
00462.caveat: The study predates much contemporary HIV care. Its results are not an individual outcome forecast and do not establish general-sarcoma benefit. A separate 14-day Kaposi trial must not be represented as the 21-day trial.

00554.title: Vinblastine and methotrexate for aggressive fibromatosis
00554.purpose: Desmoid tumours do not spread to distant organs but can grow locally, cause pain and impair function. This treatment aims to control troublesome or progressive local disease and preserve daily function; it is not a metastatic-cancer survival treatment.
00554.label: Vinblastine and methotrexate on days 1, 8 and 15; repeat every 28 days

agents.name: Vinblastine
agents.explanation: Vinblastine interferes with microtubules, preventing cells from dividing normally. Blood production, bowel movement and nerves may also be affected. It is given only into a vein by trained staff; other administration routes can be fatal.
agents.watch: Report fever, painful constipation with vomiting or abdominal swelling, new weakness or numbness, hearing changes and infusion-site pain promptly.
risks: Low blood counts with serious infection, anaemia or bleeding
Constipation, sometimes severe bowel slowing or blockage; mouth soreness, nausea and abdominal or jaw pain
Numbness, weakness and nerve injury; hearing or balance injury can occur and may persist
Hair loss, fatigue and fertility effects; severe tissue injury if the medicine leaks outside the vein
Allergic reactions and pregnancy harm; incorrect non-intravenous administration can be fatal

agents.name: Methotrexate
agents.explanation: Methotrexate interferes with folate-dependent processes needed to make genetic material and support cell growth. Mouth, bowel and blood cells can be affected. Reduced kidney clearance or fluid collections can prolong exposure and increase toxicity.
agents.watch: Report severe mouth ulcers or diarrhoea, dry cough or breathlessness, fever, yellow eyes, reduced urine or new neurological symptoms urgently. Ask the team before starting any medicine or supplement.
risks: Low blood counts, serious infection or sepsis, anaemia and bleeding
Mouth or bowel inflammation and ulceration; nausea, vomiting and diarrhoea can cause dehydration
Liver injury, including longer-term damage; kidney injury or accumulation when clearance is impaired
Lung inflammation can occur at this dose; a persistent dry cough or breathlessness requires urgent review
Rare severe skin or neurological effects and abnormal growth of immune cells (lymphoproliferative disorders); fertility and pregnancy harm
Serious medicine interactions, including with some antibiotics and painkillers; the injected oncology schedule is not a daily take-home dose

00554.schedule: Vinblastine 6 mg/m² and methotrexate 30 mg/m² are given on days 1, 8 and 15 of each 28-day cycle. Day 22 is a planned break. NCCP describes 12 cycles unless progression or unacceptable toxicity requires a change.
00554.administration: Vinblastine is given intravenously over 10 minutes and methotrexate as an intravenous bolus by trained staff. Vinblastine is for intravenous use only. The appointment also includes safety review, prescribed support and observation.
00554.baseline: Full blood count, kidney and liver tests and chest X-ray. Review mouth or bowel ulcers, breathing symptoms, infection, fluid collections, kidney function, medicines and fertility/pregnancy plans.
00554.monitoring: Full blood count and kidney/liver tests before each cycle. The team reviews current blood counts before each planned dose, including days 8 and 15, and confirms when samples are needed. Review mouth symptoms, breathing, bowel function and nerve effects before further treatment.
00554.support: Methotrexate has low and vinblastine minimal nausea/vomiting risk. NCCP lists no usual separate premedication or routine additional prophylaxis. Use individual anti-sickness, mouth and constipation support. The team prescribes any rescue medicines, extra hydration or white-cell growth-factor injections individually; the separate high-dose methotrexate support programme does not automatically apply.
00554.prep: Ask oncology/pharmacy before taking anti-inflammatory painkillers, trimethoprim or co-trimoxazole, other antibiotics, proton-pump inhibitors, folate supplements or new medicines. Avoid alcohol. Tell anaesthesia staff about methotrexate before procedures, including possible nitrous oxide use. Do not self-stop essential medicines; have the complete list reconciled.
00554.access: The team chooses appropriate intravenous access and explains its care. Report pain, burning, redness or swelling during treatment immediately. If a port or peripherally inserted central catheter is used, confirm dressing, flushing, infection precautions and eventual removal arrangements.
00554.wider: A specialist desmoid team weighs observation, systemic options, selected local treatment, symptoms, tumour location and function. Some desmoid tumours can stabilise without immediate treatment. Surgery and radiotherapy are individual decisions because local treatment can itself affect function. Discuss pain management, rehabilitation and psychological support alongside tumour control.
00554.scope: This injected regimen gives three weekly doses followed by a one-week break, for up to 12 cycles. Follow the written injection calendar; never substitute daily oral methotrexate. Kidney or liver problems, ulcers or new breathing symptoms require individual oncology/pharmacy review before further treatment. Desmoid treatment is outside the listed licensed indications of the examined vinblastine and methotrexate products. The national regimen supports this use; your team should explain the product-specific off-label rationale and document consent under local policy.
00554.trial: Methotrexate and vinblastine in advanced aggressive fibromatosis
00554.evidence: A small historical phase II study using methotrexate 30 mg/m² and vinblastine 6 mg/m² weekly found tumour shrinkage or stability and symptom benefit in some patients with advanced inoperable aggressive fibromatosis. It supports activity but had no randomised comparator.
00554.caveat: The study used continuous weekly treatment, rather than the current NCCP days 1, 8 and 15 of a 28-day cycle. DESMOPAZ used vinblastine 5 mg/m² and a different weekly-then-fortnightly schedule; its non-comparative randomised design does not establish a definitive head-to-head superiority result. Do not present trial rates as validated estimates for this exact schedule.

00554.course: 12 cycles unless the specialist changes the plan
00554.urgent: New dry cough or breathlessness, severe mouth ulcers or diarrhoea, reduced urine, jaundice, or painful constipation with vomiting or abdominal swelling requires urgent advice.
boundaries: Methotrexate kidney thresholds disagree: NCCP permits no adjustment at creatinine clearance at least 50 mL/min but also lists half dose at 20–50; the current referenced product uses above 60 full, 30–59 half and below 30 contraindicated. Exactly 50 and the 50–60 interval require reconciliation; severe impairment cannot bypass the regimen exclusion.

Methotrexate liver limits also differ narrowly: NCCP avoid above 86 micromol/L bilirubin versus current product contraindication above 85.5. Vinblastine product wording uses direct bilirubin, whereas the regimen table is less specific. Confirm the analyte and prescription.

Grade 1 mucositis calls for 50% methotrexate review; grade 2 requires a 100% reduction, meaning omit. No numeric restart formula is supplied; higher-grade disease and actual mouth/gut ulcers need separate review.
A delay of at least two weeks reduces baseline vinblastine by 25%, not methotrexate and not necessarily 25% of an already reduced dose.
Large third-space fluid collections are an exclusion because methotrexate can accumulate. Current symptoms and previous suspected drug-induced lung disease remain separate safety inputs.

tests.label: Full blood count
tests.purpose: Detect low infection-fighting cells, anaemia and bleeding risk.
tests.timing: At baseline and before each cycle as specified by NCCP. The team also reviews current blood counts before each planned dose, including days 8 and 15, and confirms when samples are needed; count recovery is required before further vinblastine.

tests.label: Kidney function and hydration
tests.purpose: Identify reduced methotrexate clearance and prevent accumulation.
tests.timing: At baseline and before each cycle; sooner for dehydration, reduced urine, vomiting, diarrhoea or new fluid collections.

tests.label: Liver tests
tests.purpose: Assess safe dosing and identify liver injury.
tests.timing: At baseline and before each cycle; repeat sooner for abnormal results or symptoms. Drug-specific source and product thresholds must be reconciled.

tests.label: Chest and breathing assessment
tests.purpose: Record baseline lung status and detect infection or drug-related inflammation.
tests.timing: Chest X-ray before treatment. Investigate a new dry cough or breathlessness promptly; routine repeated X-rays are not specified.

tests.label: Mouth and bowel review
tests.purpose: Detect methotrexate-related ulcers and vinblastine-related constipation.
tests.timing: Review before further dosing and report new symptoms between visits. Severe pain, vomiting, abdominal swelling or inability to drink needs urgent advice.

tests.label: Nerves, hearing and balance
tests.purpose: Detect effects that may require vinblastine review.
tests.timing: Ask about numbness, weakness, hearing changes or balance problems before further treatment and whenever symptoms change.

tests.label: Tumour response, symptoms and function
tests.purpose: Assess benefit separately from safety blood tests.
tests.timing: The specialist sets scan and clinical-review timing for the tumour type, treatment aim and symptoms.

anatomy: Methotrexate can cause ulcers. Report mouth sores, painful swallowing or severe diarrhoea before further treatment.
A new dry cough or breathlessness needs urgent assessment for infection or methotrexate-related lung inflammation.
Blood tests detect liver effects. Yellow eyes, dark urine or new significant upper abdominal pain needs prompt assessment.
Dehydration or kidney problems can raise methotrexate exposure. Report reduced urine, vomiting or difficulty drinking.
Low counts can cause infection, anaemia or bleeding. Fever, shaking chills or sudden illness needs immediate oncology contact.
Vinblastine can cause severe constipation. Pain, vomiting or abdominal swelling with constipation needs urgent advice.
Hair or skin changes can occur. Tell the nurse immediately about pain, burning or swelling where treatment enters the vein.
Report numbness, weakness, altered walking, hearing changes or balance problems before another vinblastine dose.
